findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy=none, pct=100, rua=true

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud against customers and vendors, creating fraud and insurability risk. Remediation is low-cost but needs mail-flow monitoring before enforcement.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, monitoring rua reports and aligning all senders first.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier=~all, lookup_count=2

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens spoofing resistance and compounds the DMARC p=none exposure for phishing impersonating the fleet platform.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all once legitimate mail flows are confirmed.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DNSSEC enabled=false on DS query for brightwaterfleet.example

findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS leaves resolution vulnerable to spoofing/cache poisoning; a hygiene gap likely noted in cyber insurance review, though not deal-blocking alone.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/ DNS provider and publish DS records, validating resolution afterwards.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern=vpn, first_seen 2023-02-11, last_seen 2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count=4
Risky hostname pattern=jenkins|old, first_seen 2021-06-03, last_seen 2026-08-14
Risky hostname pattern=staging, first_seen 2024-01-20, last_seen 2026-10-01
Risky hostname pattern=legacy, first_seen 2019-11-05, last_seen 2026-07-22

findings.deal_impact: Public VPN, legacy Jenkins, staging API, and legacy portal names signal attack surface that may be unmanaged; diligence should confirm ownership, patching, and whether these are still live pre-close.

remediation.summary: Validate each risky hostname, decommission legacy/staging systems or place behind VPN/MFA, and confirm patching.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: CT logs show unique_hostnames=47, risky_hostnames_count=4 for a 201-1000 employee company

findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for this company size suggests asset-inventory sprawl; unmanaged hosts can hide unpatched systems and complicate post-close security operations.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to an asset inventory, assign owners, and remove orphaned certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0=true, TLSv1.1=true, TLSv1.2=true; tls_versions=[TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www weakens encryption and may fail customer/insurance security questionnaires and compliance expectations.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retaining TLSv1.2+ only, and retest all hosts.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: headers strict-transport-security=null
headers strict-transport-security=null

findings.deal_impact: Without HSTS, users can be downgraded to HTTP and session data exposed; minor alone but signals basic web hardening gaps.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security header with an appropriate max-age on apex and www after confirming HTTPS-only operation.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, ExampleGate SSL-VPN version 7.0.11, match_level=product, match_tier=appliance_exposed; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.
Fingerprint product=ExampleGate SSL-VPN, version=7.0.11, kind=appliance, source=asset_path

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: an internet-facing SSL-VPN appliance fingerprinted on www matches CISA KEV at product level (version not verified). This is the top pre-close validation item due to VPN exploitation risk.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN patch/firmware level against KEV CVE, patch or isolate, and review VPN logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months=14.

findings.deal_impact: A breach 14 months ago affecting ~3,100 individuals raises regulatory, customer-notification, and insurability questions; diligence should obtain incident report, remediation proof, and any regulator follow-up.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident investigation/remediation records, confirm regulator obligations closed, and verify lessons-learned controls are in place.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: Four sampled administrative accounts bypassed MFA enforcement via legacy provisioning, increasing risk of unauthorized privileged access.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: Terminated users retained active access well beyond the 1-business-day requirement, increasing unauthorized access risk.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Security alerts were not reviewed for two consecutive weeks, creating a monitoring and incident-detection gap.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: Two emergency production changes lacked documented peer approval, weakening change-control assurance.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided

evidence.excerpt: Report period ended 2026-03-31; 213 days before 2026-10-30.

findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: Infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services..

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (Infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services.) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, contradicting 'every admin account'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: E-015 references the conditional access policy as the MFA enforcement mechanism bypassed by legacy accounts, corroborating that this enforcement mechanism exists.
3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, inconsistent with automated offboarding.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: Terminated users retained access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: For two weeks alerts were sent to a decommissioned distribution list and not reviewed, contradicting that every alert is looked at.
DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none, which is monitoring-only and not enforcement.
With DMARC p=none, F-001 states the domain can be spoofed, contradicting that nobody can spoof it.
State AG breach notice 2025-08-14 reported unauthorized access affecting approx. 3,100 individuals, contradicting 'nothing material'.
A publicly disclosed breach in 2025 involved unauthorized access to a customer support system, contradicting 'never had a breach'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back.

contradictions.explanation: CT presence alone does not prove a host is live; however legacy-portal cert last_seen 2026-07-22 and jenkins-old 2026-08-14 are within 12 months, showing active maintenance contradicting prior decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT hostnames alone do not prove live external hosts or how traffic is routed; no evidence confirms or refutes that all external access goes via the main app and VPN.
SOC 2 control CC4.1-01 was tested with no exceptions and references findings reported in the test, corroborating that a third-party test occurred.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: The last one came back clean.

contradictions.explanation: The referenced test reported 2 high-severity findings, contradicting that the last test came back clean.
Evidence states 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, directly contradicting 'no highs'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions noted, providing positive evidence supporting the backup/restore claim.

exceptions.description: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
